builder.policyAnonNoteOrganisation: Fixed to «Named» — organisations always answer attributed.
builder.policyLowText: With a threshold of {k}, answers from small groups become easier to link to individuals. The results may then count as personal data, with the deletion and access rights that entails. Consider «Named» instead if you genuinely want to see who answered.
builder.policyTwoText: At a threshold of 2, whoever answers can work out what the other person answered: they know their own answer, they see the result, and they subtract. That is not weakened anonymity — it is disclosure by arithmetic. If seeing individual answers is the point, «Med navn» is the mode that does that without promising something it cannot keep. At a threshold of 2 the aggregate is also personal data in practice.

admin.title: Administration
admin.groupThresholdNote: Groups below the threshold never get their own results
admin.roleNote: Administrators manage settings and privacy. Editors create and send surveys. Readers only see aggregated results — never individual answers.
admin.dsrDeadline: Deadline: 30 days after the request is received
admin.anonExplainer: Anonymous answers are never stored with a link to a user. The display threshold is {k} for new surveys and never lower than two, and free text is never shown with a group when the group is below the threshold. Nobody — not even an administrator — can look up who answered what.
admin.controllerNote: {company} is the data controller for the personal data. HeiTuva is the data processor and only processes data on instruction.
admin.companyNote: The organisation number and contact person are used in the data processing agreement and in the footer of the invitations respondents receive.

admin.pIpLoggingDesc: Answers cannot then be traced back to a device
admin.pEuOnly: Store data only in the EU/EEA

admin.errForbidden: You do not have permission to change this.

admin.langIntro: Change how HeiTuva reads for your organisation. Changes apply only to you, and “Reset” always brings the standard text back. Text you leave alone follows along when HeiTuva is updated.
admin.langPlaceholderMismatch: The text must use the same variables as the standard:
admin.errSsoUnavailable: Entra ID is not set up for HeiTuva yet, so sign-in cannot require it.
admin.errSsoSelf: Sign in with Entra ID yourself first, or mark yourself under “Can sign in without Entra ID” — otherwise you would be signed out on the next request.
admin.oSsoBreakGlass: Can sign in without Entra ID
admin.oSsoBreakGlassDesc: At least one active administrator must always be able to sign in with a password or email link, so the organisation can get back in if the directory fails.
admin.errSsoNoBreakGlass: First mark at least one active administrator under “Can sign in without Entra ID” — otherwise nobody could recover if Entra ID failed.
admin.errSsoLastBreakGlass: This is the last administrator who can sign in without Entra ID. Mark another one first, or turn off the Entra ID requirement.
admin.orgThresholdNote: New surveys of natural persons start at {k} answers. {k} is also the organisation’s floor: an individual survey may be set higher, not lower. The threshold can never be set below two.
admin.orgThresholdAdminOnly: Only an administrator may change a survey’s threshold, and not even an administrator may go below {k}.
admin.orgThresholdRedaktorMayLower: «Allow editors to lower the threshold» is on for the organisation: editors may change an individual survey’s threshold, and it may then be set below {k}.
admin.orgThresholdOrgSurveys: Surveys addressed to organisations have no threshold — answers are attributed to the organisation by name.
admin.thresholdTwoWarning: At a threshold of 2, whoever answers can work out what the other person answered: they know their own answer, they see the average, and they subtract. That is not weakened anonymity — it is disclosure by arithmetic.
admin.thresholdTwoAlternative: If seeing individual answers is the point, “Named” is the mode that does that without a promise it cannot keep.
admin.thresholdTwoGdpr: At a threshold of 2 the aggregate is personal data in practice. Access, rectification, erasure and retention then apply to the results, not only to the answers.
admin.brandLogoLightSpec: SVG or PNG · min. 240 px wide
admin.brandLogoDarkSpec: Used in Live and in dark e-mail
admin.brandAccentNote: The figure is the contrast between dark text (#191510) and the coloured surface. Accents are used as a surface behind dark text, never as a text colour. We do not offer a free colour picker, because arbitrary colours quickly fall below the 4.5:1 requirement.
admin.brandSenderDeferred: Sender, per-template locking and default subject lines belong on this tab, but they require a sender domain verified against the e-mail provider. They are built together with sending, not here — while nothing can be verified, a status chip would be decoration.
admin.brandTooLarge: The file is too large. Maximum 2 MB.
admin.brandWrongType: That file type is not supported. Use SVG, PNG, JPG or WebP.
admin.mgGroupsDesc: Fixed lists. Synced groups update automatically.
admin.mgSegmentsDesc: Rule-based and self-updating. Change the rule and the history is marked.
admin.mgBelowThreshold: Below the organisation’s threshold ({k}) — results are not shown
admin.mgNewDesc: Add a rule to make a segment. Without a rule it becomes a fixed group.
admin.mgCreatedSegment: The segment is created and updates itself
admin.mgDuplicate: An audience with that name already exists.
admin.mgPopulationsUnavailable: Populations — which keep customer, employee and supplier data apart, each with its own lawful basis and retention — are not built yet. Until they are, neither groups nor segments have a population, and we show none. They arrive together with lawful basis per population.
admin.mgLawfulBasisUnavailable: Lawful basis per population belongs here, but is built together with populations. We show no figures until they are real.

splash.heroBody: Most surveys die in two places: nobody bothers to answer, and the answers end up in a spreadsheet nobody opens. HeiTuva removes both. Five minutes to build, 90 seconds to answer, a finished report for your leadership team the same day.

splash.showTitle: From question to heat map to report — no spreadsheets
splash.showBody: The heat map puts every team against every question. Red is where you need to step in. Teams below the organisation's threshold are hidden automatically, and one click lifts the chart into your report.
splash.drivers1Desc: Built for the phone, no login, with the time stated before the first question. People answer because it is easier than skipping it.
splash.drivers2Desc: Nobody can see who said what — not even an administrator. Below the threshold, no numbers are shown at all.
splash.drivers3Title: You show what came of it
splash.drivers3Desc: “You asked for fewer meetings — Thursdays are now meeting-free.” Nothing lifts the next round as much.
splash.useTitle: What people actually use HeiTuva for
splash.useBody: Every template is ready to send. Change what you like, reuse wording that has been tested before, and save your own questions so the next colleague does not have to invent them again.
splash.useCases1Desc: Three to five fixed questions that show which way things are going, before anything grows.
splash.useCases2Desc: The big round, compared with last year and broken down per team.
splash.useCases3Desc: Ask new people while the impression is fresh. Sends itself after the start date.
splash.useCases4Desc: Put the QR code on the screen in the room and get answers before people head home.
splash.useCases5Desc: Ask customers right after delivery: would they recommend you, and what could have been better.
splash.useCases6Desc: One question, one link, answers within the hour. Works just as well for friends.
splash.legalTitle: Working environment, equality and supply-chain duties — documented as you go
splash.legalBody: Every duty has its template, checklist, deadline and owner. The report writes itself with method, participation, findings and actions — and is archived with a signature, so last year's version always sits right beside it.
splash.stepTitle: Four steps from question to change
splash.steps1Desc: Follow the wizard or pick a template. We flag it if a question is leading or is really two questions.
splash.steps2Desc: Pull recipients from CSV, Excel, Entra ID or Google. Send by email, SMS, link or QR.
splash.steps3Desc: All rounds in one view, a heat map per team, and the themes people write about most.
splash.steps4Desc: A report for your leadership team in one click. Tell people what you did — that is why they answer next time.
splash.priceTitle: Start free. Pay when it is worth it.
splash.priceFine: All plans: data in the EU/EEA, a data processing agreement, no numbers below the organisation's threshold, and support in Nordic languages and English. Prices excl. VAT.

splash.faq1A: Yes. We store no link between person and answer, and show no numbers below the threshold. If a team is below the threshold, not even an administrator sees it broken down.
splash.faq2A: On servers in Oslo and Frankfurt. The data processing agreement, privacy notice and risk assessment are ready in Admin, and raw data is deleted automatically after the retention period you choose.
splash.faq3Q: Do people need to log in or install anything?
splash.faq3A: No. A link, QR code or SMS opens the survey straight on their phone. One question at a time, around 90 seconds.
splash.faq4Q: Can we ask in several languages?
splash.faq4A: Yes. A survey can go out in Norwegian, Swedish, Danish and English at once — each person answers in their own language, and the answers land in the same report.
splash.faq5A: You pick a plan, or continue on the free tier. Nothing is deleted unless you ask us to.
splash.endTitle: Could you have a survey out before lunch?
splash.endBody: Free for 30 days, no card. Import recipients from CSV or Entra ID and send today.

legal.draftNotice: DRAFT — this text has not yet been reviewed by a lawyer and does not apply as an agreement until it has.
legal.privacy1P: HeiTuva is provided by Nordisk Studio AS, Storgata 12, 0155 Oslo, Norway. For organisations that use HeiTuva to ask their employees, the organisation is the controller and Nordisk Studio AS is the processor. This notice explains what we do with data in both roles.
legal.privacy2H: What we process about you as someone who administers HeiTuva
legal.privacy2P:
When you create an account we store your name, work email, your organisation's name and your role. We also keep a log of actions that change settings, roles and privacy choices (the audit log), so the organisation can document who did what. We do not store IP addresses or browser information tied to you.

The basis is the agreement with your organisation (GDPR art. 6(1)(b)) and our legitimate interest in securing the service (art. 6(1)(f)).
legal.privacy3H: What we process about you as someone answering a survey
legal.privacy3P:
When you answer anonymously the answer is stored without any link to you: no invitation ID, no user, no IP address, and the time is rounded to the hour. The database has a technical constraint that prevents an anonymous answer from ever being tied to a person. The organisation sees results only once enough people in the same group have answered — never below the organisation's threshold, which is never lower than two — and free text is never shown together with a group below that threshold.

When a survey is set to “with name”, you see that clearly before answering, and your answer is stored with your name. Your invitation link is personal and stored only as a hash; it cannot be reconstructed from the database.

Surveys addressed to organisations — supplier due diligence under the Transparency Act, for example — are a different case: you answer on behalf of the organisation, the answer is attributed to it by name, and no threshold applies. The survey says so before you answer.
legal.privacy4P: All data is stored in the EU/EEA: the database with Supabase in Frankfurt (eu-central-1), the application with Vercel in EU regions, email via Amazon SES in Stockholm (eu-north-1), SMS via LINK Mobility (Nordics), error reporting via Sentry in the EU. No personal data is transferred outside the EEA.
legal.privacy5P: Answers are deleted after the organisation's chosen retention period (24 months by default) by an automatic job. Account data is deleted when the organisation ends the agreement, after a 30-day grace period. The audit log is kept for the life of the agreement, because it is the organisation's documentation.
legal.privacy6P:
You have the right of access, rectification, erasure and data portability, and to object to processing based on legitimate interest. For data your organisation processes about you, contact the organisation; we help them answer within the deadlines. For data we process as controller, contact personvern@heituva.no. You may complain to Datatilsynet.

Anonymous answers cannot be found for you — that is the whole point of their being anonymous.
legal.privacy7P: Supabase (database, sign-in, storage — Frankfurt), Vercel (hosting — EU), Amazon Web Services (email — Stockholm), LINK Mobility (SMS — Norway), Cloudflare (bot protection on the front page), Sentry (error reporting — EU). The full list with purposes is in the data processing agreement.
legal.privacy8P: Nordisk Studio AS, Storgata 12, 0155 Oslo, Norway. personvern@heituva.no.
legal.dpa1P: This agreement is between the organisation using HeiTuva (the controller) and Nordisk Studio AS (the processor), and covers all processing the processor carries out on the controller's behalf in HeiTuva. The purpose is running employee surveys and the statutory documentation under the Working Environment Act, the Transparency Act and the Equality and Anti-Discrimination Act.
legal.dpa2H: Nature of the processing and categories
legal.dpa2P: Categories of data subjects: employees and others the organisation invites. Categories of data: name, email, mobile number, group membership, survey answers (anonymous or named at the organisation's choice), and free text. Special categories may occur in free text; the processor handles them only as part of the answer and not for its own purposes.
legal.dpa3P: The processor processes data only on documented instructions from the controller. The settings in HeiTuva (anonymity, retention, who has access) are such instructions. The processor notifies without delay if, in its view, an instruction infringes data protection law.
legal.dpa4P: Persons processing data at the processor are bound by confidentiality. Technical measures include: row-level security in the database separating organisations from one another; a threshold before any result is shown for a group of natural persons, enforced in the database — the organisation's own threshold, never lower than two; no threshold applies to surveys addressed to organisations, where the answer is attributed to the organisation by name; anonymous answers stored without any link to a person, enforced by a database constraint; invitation links stored only as hashes; encryption in transit and at rest; an append-only audit log; daily backups with point-in-time recovery.
legal.dpa5P: The controller gives general authorisation for the sub-processors listed in the privacy notice: Supabase Inc. (database, sign-in, storage — Frankfurt, EU), Vercel Inc. (application hosting — EU regions), Amazon Web Services EMEA SARL (email delivery — Stockholm), LINK Mobility AS (SMS — Oslo), Cloudflare Inc. (bot protection on the front page, no answer data), Functional Software Inc. / Sentry (error reporting — EU, without free text). The processor gives 30 days' notice of new sub-processors; the controller may object within that period.
legal.dpa6P: Data is stored and processed in the EU/EEA. No transfer to third countries takes place as part of the service.
legal.dpa7P: The processor assists the controller in meeting data subjects' rights (access, rectification, erasure, portability) through the tools under Administration → Privacy and GDPR, and on request. In the event of a personal data breach the processor notifies the controller without undue delay and at the latest within 24 hours of becoming aware, with the information article 33(3) requires, in phases if necessary.
legal.dpa8P: The controller may request documentation of compliance and may, once a year with 30 days' notice, carry out or commission an independent audit.
legal.dpa9P: This agreement runs for the life of the customer agreement. On termination all personal data is deleted no later than 30 days after the controller has exported it, unless law requires longer retention. A signed version of this agreement with the organisation's name and date is issued at contract and is available under Administration → Privacy and GDPR → Documentation.
